newsitem.title: USA: CME adopts policy to let firms deploy technology.
newsitem.headline: CME adopts policy to let firms deploy technology.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) said it will "unfetter" firms and allow them to deploy new technology on CME trading floors, the CME announced Monday.

The exchange said it adopted a new policy last week to expedite implementation of new technology and allow CME's members and member firms to deploy whatever technological innovations they think will enhance open outcry markets.
"We believe strongly in the ability of this membership to develop innovative technology supporting open outcry and enhancing our competitive edge," said CME Chairman Jack Sandner in a press release.
"This policy is intended to unleash that creative potential and to enable more rapid deployment of technology that will be of most benefit to the people who actually use it," Sandner said.
The CME's role will be to provide its facilities and set certain minimum standards so that different uses of technology do not interfere with each other, the exchange said.
